input.reasoning:
Estimate derived from story points using a standard planning-poker conversion (1 point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended engineering effort, adjusted per task type), then split across roles based on task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, QA, DevOps). Total backlog = 81 points. No historical actuals exist for this team/project, so effort-per-point is an assumption calibrated from typical SaaS portal builds of similar complexity (auth, RBAC, payments, data migration). Role hours were sanity-checked against available FTE capacity over an assumed ~3-month (12-week) delivery window:
- Backend Developer: 1.5 FTE x 12 weeks x 40h = 720h capacity
- Frontend Developer: 1.0 FTE x 12 weeks x 40h = 480h capacity
- QA Engineer: 0.6 FTE x 12 weeks x 40h = 288h capacity
- DevOps Engineer: 0.4 FTE x 12 weeks x 40h = 192h capacity

Allocated hours were kept within these envelopes, with DevOps and QA flagged as tight given the backlog (data migration, payments webhooks, and CI setup all compete for the same thin DevOps/QA capacity).

Task-level effort logic:
- PW-1 (CI/staging, 5pts, High): DevOps-led, some Backend support. ~40h DevOps + 16h Backend.
- PW-2 (Design system, 8pts, Medium): Frontend-heavy. ~120h Frontend + 16h QA.
- PW-3 (Registration/login, 8pts, Urgent): Backend-heavy with Frontend and QA. ~70h Backend + 40h Frontend + 20h QA.
- PW-4 (RBAC, 13pts, High): Backend + Frontend + QA, cross-cutting. ~90h Backend + 50h Frontend + 24h QA.
- PW-5 (Dashboard, 8pts, High): Frontend-led with Backend API work. ~40h Backend + 70h Frontend + 16h QA.
- PW-6 (Invoice list/detail, 5pts, Medium): Balanced Backend/Frontend. ~40h Backend + 40h Frontend + 12h QA.
- PW-7 (Stripe integration, 13pts, Urgent): Backend + DevOps (webhooks) + QA (reconciliation testing). ~110h Backend + 20h Frontend + 30h QA + 24h DevOps.
- PW-8 (Legacy migration, 21pts, High): Backend + DevOps heavy, QA validation. ~160h Backend + 40h DevOps + 40h QA.

Summed and rounded to role totals: Backend 526h, Frontend 340h, QA 142h, DevOps 104h. All within FTE capacity envelopes (Backend well within 720h, Frontend within 480h, QA within 288h, DevOps within 192h), though QA and DevOps remain the tightest constraints relative to the risk profile of payments and migration work — flagged as a risk requiring either scope reduction, timeline extension, or temporary contractor support.

Non-labour costs include Stripe sandbox/production fees, staging/cloud infrastructure for CI and migration dry-runs, and a data migration validation/reconciliation tooling allowance.

Scenarios (P50/P70/P90) reflect uncertainty typical for a project with no historical actuals: P50 is the base build as scoped, P70 adds ~15% contingency for integration and migration rework, P90 adds ~30% for material schedule/scope risk (e.g., migration data quality issues, Stripe compliance review delays).

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees, sandbox testing, and compliance review support
Staging/CI cloud infrastructure (environments, pipelines) for project duration
Legacy data migration tooling, validation scripts, and Oracle export/connectivity licensing
Contingency buffer for third-party/API rate changes and misc tooling

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; effort-per-story-point and role splits are estimated from comparable SaaS portal projects, not measured data.
Assumed delivery window of ~12 weeks, used only to sanity-check that allocated hours per role stay within available FTE capacity.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended effort, adjusted per task based on which roles are actually involved.
QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) capacity is thin relative to the backlog's testing and infrastructure/migration needs; this is a scheduling risk, not just a cost one.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) is treated as primarily a Backend + DevOps effort with QA validation, excluding any DBA-specific role since none is staffed on this project.
Non-labour costs are rough allowances for Stripe fees, cloud/staging infrastructure, and migration tooling; actual vendor quotes were not available.
All 8 backlog items are assumed in-scope for this estimate; descoping or deferring lower-priority items would reduce the total as shown in the reductions section.

reductions.description: Defer PW-2 (Design system and component library, Medium priority) to a later phase and use a minimal off-the-shelf Angular Material theme instead of a custom component library for MVP.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend hours by ~120h and QA hours by ~16h; delays a polished design system until post-launch.

reductions.description: Descope PW-6 (Invoice list and detail view, Medium priority) from this phase, shipping a simpler read-only invoice table without PDF download initially.
reductions.effect: Removes ~40h Backend, ~40h Frontend, ~12h QA; PDF export and filtering added in a later release.

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours on PW-4 (RBAC) by relying more on automated test coverage built during PW-3, rather than a full separate QA pass.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~20h of QA Engineer time; slightly increases regression risk on permission edge cases.

reductions.description: Defer non-critical migration tooling/licensing spend by reusing existing open-source ETL scripts instead of purchasing a commercial Oracle connectivity tool.
reductions.effect: Reduces non-labour migration tooling line from $4,000 to $1,500; requires more Backend engineering time to build custom scripts (not separately costed here).
